requirements.requirement: Keep the installed curl package at its current version when system updates are performed on node1.
requirements.summary: curl was initially installed at 7.47.0-1ubuntu2.19 without a hold. The executor applied an APT hold, and both APT and dpkg then reported the held state. Simulated upgrades before and after a verified reboot completed successfully with zero curl installation actions; curl remained installed and functional at the original version.

overall_summary: The task outcome is satisfied. curl remained at 7.47.0-1ubuntu2.19 under a persistent package hold, and upgrade simulations scheduled no curl change. The provider-wide restart protocol is also well evidenced: the pre-restart identity and healthy state were captured, restart scheduling was acknowledged, connection failures bounded the disruption, the boot ID changed, and package/curl health recovered. Fixed lifecycle observations independently confirm the boot-ID transition.
limitations: No real package upgrade was executed; update behavior was tested with successful apt-get simulated upgrades. The persistent APT/dpkg hold and consistent pre/post-restart results make this a minor evidence limitation rather than an outcome failure.
There is no cluster state to validate because the managed topology contains one standalone node.

operational_hygiene.summary: The intended hold and mandatory restart were appropriately scoped, and node1 finished with clean package state, no failed services, and no added listening sockets. No causally unrelated state-changing experiments were identified. However, the final upgrade simulation in cmd-08ef0a9f839b4c98 left /tmp/curl-hold-post-reboot-sim.txt behind; it was a legitimate evidence artifact but was not cleaned up. The earlier simulation file from cmd-0f3b91d49e604432 did not remain after reboot.
